subject: Re: ZenChat MSA redline — Usage definition (tokens/retries/caching) + dispute/credits
body:
From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@zenchat.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evan Ross <evan.ross@zenchat.com>, Outside Counsel (ZenChat) <legal@hathawayllp.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: ZenChat MSA redline — Usage definition (tokens/retries/caching) + dispute/credits

Michael,

As discussed, sending our redline focused on usage measurement and billing dispute mechanics. Our main concerns are (a) token counting ambiguity across endpoints and (b) scenarios where retries/failover/caching could cause double charges.

Key asks (also marked in the redline):
1) Define “Token” and “Usage” with enough specificity (including which tokenizer, what counts as prompt vs completion, and treatment of tool/function calls).
2) Confirm that tokens generated during server-side retries/fallback are not billed twice.
3) Clarify whether cached responses are billed (and if so, at what rate / how disclosed).
4) Dispute window: proposing 60 days from invoice date, and suspension of collection on disputed amounts.
5) Credits/refunds: we asked for a credit commitment where metering defects are identified.

Attachments:
- ZenChat_Redline_Redwood_MSA_v7_2026-02-10.docx
- ZenChat_Redline_OrderForm_HostedAPI_Dedicated_v3_2026-02-10.docx

Thanks,
Priya

Priya Desai
Head of Procurement
ZenChat

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@zenchat.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Evan Ross <evan.ross@zenchat.com>, Outside Counsel (ZenChat) <legal@hathawayllp.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: ZenChat MSA redline — Usage definition (tokens/retries/caching) + dispute/credits

Priya — received, thank you.

We agree the usage definition needs to be crisp, especially around retries/failover and caching. We’ll turn comments quickly.

At a high level (not legal language yet):
- Tokenization: we can define “Tokens” as the units counted by the applicable model’s tokenizer at the time the request is processed, and we can point to the “usage” fields in the API response / usage export as the measurement source.
- Retries/fallback: our intent is not to double-bill for server-side retries/fallback attempts for the same request; metering is tied to a request identifier/idempotency behavior.
- Caching: today we disclose billed tokens separately from raw tokens, and we can clarify contractually that cached outputs are treated as usage only to the extent they are billable per the Order Form (and that the customer usage export will reflect cache-hit attribution).

We’ll propose specific clause language and send back by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Michael

Michael Grant
General Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 12:21 PM PST
Subject: Re: ZenChat MSA redline — Usage definition (tokens/retries/caching) + dispute/credits

Michael — flagging the key pressure points from their redline that we should address explicitly:

1) They want us to specify an exact tokenizer algorithm/version. That’s hard to freeze (models change). Maybe define as “as reported by Redwood in usage metrics for the applicable model version,” and commit to notice if measurement method changes in a way that materially impacts charges.

2) They proposed suspension of payment for disputed amounts + 60-day dispute window. Our standard is 30 days from invoice receipt; we can consider 45 for them but not suspend full invoice payments.

3) Credits: we can agree to credit for “verifiable overbilling attributable to Redwood metering error” and cap it (or tie to the dispute resolution section).

Nikhil can confirm technical language re: tool calls and caching attribution fields.

-Sofia

Sofia Mendes
Commercial Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 1:08 PM PST
Subject: Re: ZenChat MSA redline — Usage definition (tokens/retries/caching) + dispute/credits

Adding RevRec lens:

- Avoid committing to retroactive invoice recalculation broadly. We can do credits for confirmed meter defects, but should keep language tight: “reasonable investigation,” “supported by Redwood records,” and “credited on a future invoice.”

- Any clause that implies the customer’s logs control over Redwood’s ledger creates audit risk. We should keep “usage as measured by Redwood” as source of truth, with a right to request supporting detail (usage exports) during the dispute window.

- For late-arriving usage events: we should avoid complicated exceptions in contract. If needed, we can state invoices reflect usage recorded through the close of the billing period per our standard reporting cutoffs, and material corrections handled via credit memo.

Emily

Emily Stone
Accounting / Revenue Recognition
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@zenchat.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evan Ross <evan.ross@zenchat.com>, Outside Counsel (ZenChat) <legal@hathawayllp.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 9:37 AM PST
Subject: Re: ZenChat MSA redline — Usage definition (tokens/retries/caching) + dispute/credits

Michael,

Thanks. Two quick clarifications before you send the markup:

1) If you don’t specify the tokenizer/version, how do we ensure token counting won’t change mid-term? We need predictability for forecasting.

2) For retries/fallback: we’d like an explicit statement that “unsuccessful attempts” (including timeouts and internal retries) are not billable. If a response is partially streamed and then retried, is any portion billed?

3) For caching: if a response is served from cache, are we billed for the tokens “returned” (even if the model did not run)? If yes, we’d want that in the Order Form and clearly exposed in reporting.

Separately, Evan is asking if you can provide sample usage export fields (or a schema) showing billed vs raw tokens and cache hit attribution.

Priya

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@zenchat.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Evan Ross <evan.ross@zenchat.com>, Outside Counsel (ZenChat) <legal@hathawayllp.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 1:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: ZenChat MSA redline — Usage definition (tokens/retries/caching) + dispute/credits

Priya — answering inline, and we’ll follow with proposed contract language.

1) Tokenizer/version predictability
We can’t practically freeze a single tokenizer across all models because tokenization is model-dependent and customers can select/upgrade model versions. What we can do:
- Define that Tokens/Usage are measured as reported in Redwood’s usage metrics for the applicable model/version used to process the request.
- Add a notice commitment for changes to our usage measurement methodology that would reasonably be expected to materially impact charges (e.g., changes in what we count as billable tokens, not routine model improvements).

2) Retries/fallback and partial streaming
Commercial intent: you should not pay twice for the same request due to Redwood-side retries/failover.
- Unsuccessful attempts (internal retries where no customer-visible output is delivered) are not billable.
- If partial output is delivered to the client and the request later fails, the parties can treat the delivered portion as billable usage. (We can tighten this to “only tokens successfully delivered to the customer are billable,” subject to how streaming is accounted in the API usage fields.)
Nikhil is confirming exact phrasing that maps to how the usage export reports “billed tokens” on streaming responses.

3) Caching
We’ll make this explicit in the Order Form: whether cache-served outputs are billable and how they’re shown in reporting.
Our current standard approach is:
- Usage reporting includes cache attribution (cache_hit true/false) and billed_tokens.
- If cache-served outputs are billed, they are billed based on billed_tokens returned to you, and the usage export will reflect that it was a cache hit.
(If you want cache-served outputs to be non-billable, that’s a commercial packaging question; we can route to Sales/RevOps, but it’s not typical for most usage-based APIs.)

Usage export schema
We can share a sample schema excerpt in writing. At minimum: request_id, timestamp, model, region, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, billed_tokens, cache_hit, and retry_count (where available).

More to follow shortly in the redline.

Best,
Michael

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@zenchat.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Evan Ross <evan.ross@zenchat.com>, Outside Counsel (ZenChat) <legal@hathawayllp.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 4:38 PM PST
Subject: Re: ZenChat MSA redline — Usage definition (tokens/retries/caching) + dispute/credits

Priya,

Attached is proposed language for the MSA + conforming edits we suggest for the Order Form. (We’ll also incorporate these into your redline doc if you prefer markup format.)

Attachment:
- Redwood_Usage_Definition_Proposed_Language_2026-02-11.docx

Summary of proposed changes (plain English):

A) Definitions (MSA)
- “Tokens” = units as measured by Redwood’s systems for the applicable model/version used to process the request.
- “Usage” = the billable units reported in the Redwood usage records (including billed_tokens and any other billable measures specified in the Order Form).
- Tool/function calls and structured outputs: tokens are counted consistently as reflected in the API usage fields (prompt + completion) and summed into billed_tokens.

B) Retries/failover
- We added an explicit statement that Redwood will not charge twice for server-side retries/fallback for the same request.
- Billable usage is limited to tokens successfully delivered in the response to Customer (including in streaming), as reflected in Redwood’s usage records.

C) Caching
- We moved “cache-served responses” into an Order Form disclosure concept: if billable, billed_tokens apply and cache_hit will be visible in reporting.
- If you want cache-served responses to be non-billable, we can reflect that as an Order Form commercial term (but would need sign-off; not a standard default).

D) Disputes and credits
- Dispute window: we proposed 45 days from invoice date (instead of 60).
- Payment: undisputed portions remain payable on time.
- If Redwood confirms an overcharge due to a metering defect, Redwood will issue a credit on a future invoice (or credit memo) for the verified overbilled amounts.

If helpful, we can jump on a 30-min call with you + counsel tomorrow to walk through the definition language.

Regards,
Michael

Michael Grant
General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Laura Bennett (CFO) and Emily Stone (RevRec) cc’d for visibility on credit/dispute mechanics.
